label: copy-phase outputs of length-3 sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and almost entirely in the shortest sequences (L=3: 88% of activation mass, 62.7x lift). It fires at t=4 and t=5, which output original tokens 1 and 2. The last step (t=5, outputting the final token) is the most frequent and holds 63% of the mass, against 25% at t=4. It never fires during the original phase or on the <DEL> step. Only about half of L=3 copy steps are active. Input-token identity shifts the rate somewhat (i, d, c, f and 3 fire more often; w, p, g, k and y less often), but no clean token rule separates the active steps from the inactive ones. Outside L=3 there are weak, scattered activations: L=4 at t=6 (recall_idx 2) and L=9 near t=12 and t=17. These hold about 12% of the mass.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=12: i, d, x, z; t=13: i, d, x, h; t=11: i, d, x, z) and the previous input (most: j, 1, q, u, c, n; least: r, x, h, k); timing cues that raise it most: L=3, L=3 & t=5, L=3 & t=4.
